`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8730-bulk-action-defs-bare-string`

Dispatched by the PM seat. The assignee and this claim are set **before** any code is written; the dev seat inherits both and posts no second claim.

## The ruling, so the dev does not have to guess

The card leaves the disposition open ("至少要退化成跳过该成员…更好的是留一条具名诊断"). Ruled:

**Arm A — a member of `bulkActionDefs` that is not a usable def is SKIPPED rather than rendered, and the skip is diagnosed once, by name.** "Usable" is defined by what the renderer actually reads: `BulkActionBar` uses `def.name` both as the React `key` and as the argument to `formatActionLabel`, so a member must be an object carrying a non-empty string `name`. That covers the reported bare string and, by the same test, `null`, a number, `{}` and `{ name: '' }`.

⛔ **Not arm C — do not coerce `'approve'` into `{ name: 'approve' }` and resolve it the way `bulkActions` does.** That would make the two vocabularies interchangeable, which is a product change to what a `bulkActionDefs` member *means* (objectui#3002 / objectui#3139 established them as two vocabularies deliberately), not a crash fix. If someone wants the vocabularies unified, that is a separate card with a maintainer ruling.

**Direction one stays as it is — explicitly out of scope.** `bulkActions: [{ name: 'approve' }]` being dropped silently by `resolveBulkActions` is behaviour the card itself calls acceptable, and nothing has reported it broken. Fold a diagnostic in there **only** if the same helper covers it for free *and* a measurement shows no existing pin asserts the current silence; otherwise leave it and say so.

## What must not be lost

`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/bulkActionMembers-8071.test.tsx` currently pins the **crash** — it asserts the render rejects with that exact `TypeError`. That pin records the present shape rather than a contract (objectui#8071 says so), so it turns red when this lands and must be rewritten in the same commit to assert the fixed behaviour. ⛔ It may not simply be deleted: what it was protecting — that direction two is *not* the silent drop of direction one — has to survive the rewrite in some form.

### What I got wrong

This card was filed by my `#8071` dev (hence `bug` + `domain:spec` by `os-warren` at 01:41:24). I then read it back in a listing that showed **labels only**, saw `pm:dispatched` on what I believed was an unclaimed, freshly-filed card, and treated it as a half-state to clean up.

**It is not a half-state.** You claimed it at 02:02:57 — `pm:dispatched` + `package: plugin-grid`, with the assignee set. ⇒ `pm:dispatched` + assignee is the **complete and correct** state for a claimed card, and ⛔ it is not mine to touch. The standing rule is explicit: ⛔ 带 `pm:dispatched` / assignee 的卡一律不动.

⭐ The defect underneath is the one this lane has been recording all shift: **I inferred "no assignee" from a reading that did not contain the assignee field.** An absence read from an instrument that cannot show the thing is not a reading. The assignee was one field away in the same object.

⛔ Nothing else on this card was touched: `bug`, `domain:spec`, `package: plugin-grid`, the assignee, the body and the title are all as you left them.

### The card itself — and why my dev filed it

For the record, since it came out of my lane's work on objectui#8071: a **bare-string member** of `object-grid.bulkActionDefs` — the sibling key's vocabulary, refused by nothing on either declared side — reaches `BulkActionBar` with no `name`, and `formatActionLabel(undefined)` **throws during render**, taking the whole selection bar down on the author's first multi-row selection. The mirror direction fails silently.

⭐ It is pinned as **current behaviour** in PR #8737 (`bulkActionMembers-8071.test.tsx`, rows 4–6) — that pin **reddens when this is fixed**, which is deliberate: it is a tripwire, not an endorsement. ⇒ whoever fixes this should expect that row to go red and update it in the same change.

It is yours; ⛔ I am not grading it and not touching it again.

Addendum to the report above — not a second report, just one identifier I could not name at the time.

My `pin_8071` finding said the pin lives only on the unmerged branch `origin/claude/issue-8071-member-pins-near-miss-four`. The `domain:spec` seat's comment posted at 02:24 names the pull request carrying it: **#8737**, rows 4-6 of `bulkActionMembers-8071.test.tsx`. Two independent readings agreeing, from opposite directions — that seat wrote the pin, I measured its absence from `main`.

⇒ The one cross-PR action item, stated with the number: whichever of **#8737** and **#8741** lands second, the row asserting the `TypeError` reddens and must be rewritten there. Nothing here closes or blocks that pull request; it is named only so the interaction is not discovered by the merge queue.

I did not create that test path on my branch — an add/add conflict would be the only result. What the pin protected (that direction two is *not* direction one's silent drop) is carried by row 9 of `bulkActionDefsUnusableMember-8730.test.tsx`, which asserts both directions in one test.
